intro: Game suggestions built from the gaps, trends, outliers and go-to-market research in this atlas. They're ranked for your model by default: one person building with AI, games playable from a link, marketing on TikTok and YouTube. Switch the scoring to 'Small studio, Steam' to see the flagship-style ideas rise.
caveat: No dataset can guarantee a hit, and most games, web or Steam, earn very little. Each suggestion is a bet backed by specific signals, with gates that tell you early whether it's working. The scores are research-based judgements, so treat close scores as ties.

concepts.name: Treat Box
concepts.niche: Daily collectible · blind-box reveal · little treats
concepts.hook: Open one free mystery box a day. Collect plush little treats with faces. Find the secret one.
concepts.oneLiner: A daily free 'blind box' of tiny plush-style treats (a mochi, a croissant, a matcha latte with a face) that you collect, name and arrange on your shelf.
concepts.pitch: Blind boxes are the consumer craze of the decade (Pop Mart's revenue rose 185% in 2025 on Labubu), adults buy cute collectibles for themselves, and unboxing is one of the most-watched video formats. Treat Box gives people the reveal without the price: one free box a day, series of six treats plus one secret with the odds shown openly, and a shelf to arrange your collection on. The treats look like Jellycat plush food, the cast is your own, and every opening is a 10-second clip.

concepts.name: Tea Cart
concepts.hook: Start with one tea cart. Brew, serve, hire helpers, and grow it into a little tea street.
concepts.oneLiner: A walk-and-serve idle shop game: brew tea, serve cute customers, hire helpers and expand from a cart to a whole street.
concepts.pitch: On Poki, the Cozy category is led by idle shop games like Monkey Mart and My Perfect Hotel, and idle/clicker mobile revenue grew 40% in H1 2025. Good Pizza, Great Pizza reached 300M+ downloads with a 12-person team, earning about 60% from ads and 40% from purchases. Tea Cart is a portal-native idle shop with a warm identity: tea from around the world, regular customers with small stories, and a street that grows as you play. On Steam, shop sims are flooding (the Shop Keeper tag is up 634%), but on the web this is the genre players are already looking for.

concepts.name: Pond Party
concepts.hook: Send a link, and your friends are fishing next to you in seconds. No download.
concepts.oneLiner: A tiny browser hangout where friends fish together, show off catches, and sit by the water. One link joins a pond.
concepts.pitch: Webfishing (solo developer, est. 1.0–2.1M copies) proved a cozy fishing hangout spreads through friend groups and funny clips. fly.pieter.com proved a browser multiplayer game that starts from a link can make serious money fast. Pond Party joins them: open a link, pick a little critter, and you're at a pond with friends. Fish, trade, decorate the dock, and react with preset emotes. It's safe by design: no open voice or text chat, which matters for cozy players who are tired of toxic spaces.

Petal Drop takes that proven loop and gives it a cozy identity: hand-painted flowers, soft physics, a garden that fills with everything you've bloomed, and a daily seeded pot with a shareable bloom card. It's the fastest game here to build and the easiest to clip.

concepts.hook: One cozy mess a day. Tidy it, then share your result without spoilers.
concepts.oneLiner: A new little scene to tidy every day: a desk, a picnic, a sewing box. Put things where they belong and share your result card.
concepts.pitch: Wordle showed that one short daily puzzle with a spoiler-free result spreads on its own, and the New York Times now counts billions of solves a year. A Little to the Left and Unpacking showed that tidying is one of the most satisfying things to watch in a clip. Daily Tidy puts the two together: one hand-made cozy scene a day, a few minutes to solve, and a result card ('🧺 tidied in 4 moves, 1 hint') players paste into group chats. Every day's scene is also a ready-made TikTok: 'today's Daily Tidy, can you do it in fewer moves?'

concepts.name: Driftgarden
concepts.niche: Cozy survival-lite crafting · co-op 1–4 · ocean setting
concepts.oneLiner: Grow a floating garden-boat with up to three friends and sail a flooded, sunlit archipelago. No death, no hunger bars, no rush.
concepts.pitch: The islands have slipped beneath a gentle sea. You and your friends tend a houseboat that is also a garden: plant on the deck, fish over the rail, salvage sunken cottages, and graft new rooms onto the hull as it grows. Each island has a small community to help and a biome to bring back to life. It keeps survival-craft's 'gather, craft, expand, explore' loop, the best-performing niche in the research, removes everything punishing, and is built for co-op from day one.
concepts.audience: Friend groups and couples aged 18–40 who play Stardew, Dinkum or Webfishing together and bounced off Raft or Valheim as too stressful. Also solo cozy players who want exploration beyond a farm.
concepts.sessionLength: 30–90 minutes; one in-game day at sea takes about 20 minutes
concepts.artDirection: Bright stylized 3D with a watercolor sea and chunky, readable silhouettes. The capsule should say 'a garden on a boat' at thumbnail size.

demand.why: Cozy crafting/survival-lite and co-op 2–4 both score demand 9. 28% of open-world survival-craft games reach 1,000 reviews, the best of 23 niches measured.

gap.why: Survival-lite supply is 5 and ocean settings are 3, against farming at 9. Few games combine no-death survival with co-op and the sea.

scopeFit.why: 3D plus online co-op is the hardest scope in this list. Feasible for 5–6 people over about 24 months with peer-to-peer networking and no servers, but it needs a network programmer.

monetization.why: Supports a $19.99 price, friend 4-packs, a supporter pack and paid expansions. Co-op means each sale tends to pull in more sales.

marketability.why: Co-op chaos and boat-building make great clips and streams. 'Garden on a boat' reads instantly.

momentum.why: Co-op keywords and cozy survival-crafting are both rising among successful Steam games; Webfishing and Dinkum show friend-group cozy selling.

soloSpeed.why: 3D online co-op with a sailing world is the heaviest build here, even with AI writing code; art and netcode testing take months.

instantPlay.why: A 3D online co-op game is a Steam download, not a tap-to-play link.

culture.why: Loneliness and third-place trends favor co-op, but few culture signals point at survival or the sea.

The boat is your home: building and decorating happen on something that travels.

concepts.niche: Cozy co-op for couples · non-Western setting · shop sim
concepts.oneLiner: Run a night-market food stall with your partner: one cooks, one shops and serves, and nobody gets yelled at.
concepts.pitch: A two-player co-op game set in an East or Southeast Asian night market. Pick a culture your team knows first-hand. Each evening one player cooks while the other buys ingredients, chats with regulars and decorates the stall. Regulars bring small stories; market families teach you recipes. It has Overcooked's teamwork without the timer stress, the warmth of Venba and Wanderstop, and shop-sim progression. A Friend's Pass lets the second player join free, so every copy sold recruits another player.

concepts.name: Terraces
concepts.niche: Relaxing builder · non-Western setting · clip-able toy
concepts.hook: Carve a mountain into terraces and watch water, rice and villages find their way down.
concepts.oneLiner: Sculpt a misty mountainside into terraced fields. Water cascades from step to step, and villages grow wherever it reaches.
concepts.pitch: A relaxing builder inspired by the rice terraces of Southeast Asia and the Andes, made with people from those places. You don't place buildings: you shape the land. Cut a terrace and water spills down to fill it; plant along the flow and a hamlet appears. Each mountain is a gentle puzzle about where water goes, with no fail state and no timer. It takes Tiny Glade's lesson (an action that's satisfying in five seconds markets itself) and Dorfromantik's light goals, and puts them somewhere builders haven't been.
